question: How long is a standard Louisiana boat registration valid before it must be renewed?
choice_b: Three years from the date it was issued
explanation: LDWF boat registrations are valid for three years from their date of issuance, after which the owner must renew.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: If a Louisiana boat registration is not renewed on time, what is the grace period before the registration is canceled?
choice_a: There is no grace period; it cancels the day it expires
explanation: Owners have 60 days after the expiration date to renew a lapsed Louisiana boat registration before LDWF cancels it.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: When LDWF approves a boat registration, what does it issue to the owner?
choice_a: A single decal only, with no certificate
choice_b: A metal license plate similar to a vehicle
choice_c: Nothing physical; registration exists only in a digital database
choice_d: A registration certificate and two decals
explanation: LDWF issues a registration certificate stating the assigned number, along with two decals that must be affixed to the vessel.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: Where should a boat's LDWF-issued registration number and decals be affixed?
choice_a: On the boat, painted or attached according to LDWF specifications
choice_b: Only on the trailer, never on the boat itself
choice_c: Registration numbers and decals are optional to display
choice_d: Inside a locked cabin where they cannot be seen from outside
explanation: Owners must paint or attach the assigned registration number to the vessel and affix the LDWF-issued decals according to LDWF's placement specifications, so the vessel can be identified.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: The Louisiana boat registration certificate should be kept:
choice_a: Posted publicly on a dock bulletin board
choice_b: Onboard the vessel at all times, preferably in a waterproof container
choice_c: At the owner's residence only, never aboard the boat
choice_d: Mailed back to LDWF once the vessel is registered
explanation: LDWF advises keeping the registration certificate onboard at all times, preferably in a waterproof container, so it is available if requested during an inspection or after an incident.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: Which of the following vessels requires titling in Louisiana in addition to registration?
choice_a: A vessel used exclusively on private ponds
choice_b: Titling never applies in Louisiana; only registration exists
choice_c: A homemade vessel, or a boat/outboard motor of 25 horsepower or more that is financed or already titled in another state
choice_d: Any canoe under 10 feet in length
explanation: Louisiana requires titling -- separate from ordinary registration -- for homemade vessels and for boats/outboard motors of 25 hp or more that are financed, already titled elsewhere, or have an incorrect HIN.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: What is the fee for a new or transfer boat title in Louisiana, per LDWF's published fee schedule?
choice_c: There is no fee for titling in Louisiana
explanation: LDWF's published titling fee is $26 for both a new title and a title transfer.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: A Louisiana boat owner can renew their registration through which of the following methods?
choice_a: In person at LDWF headquarters, by mail, or online
choice_b: Only by visiting LDWF headquarters in person
choice_c: Only through a licensed marine dealer
choice_d: Registration renewal is not offered directly through LDWF
explanation: LDWF offers multiple renewal channels for boat registration: in person at headquarters, by mail, or online.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: To title a boat in Louisiana, an owner generally must submit which documentation?
choice_a: No documentation is required to obtain a Louisiana boat title
choice_b: A completed Boat Registration/Boat and Motor Title Application along with original ownership documentation
choice_c: Only a verbal statement of ownership, with nothing in writing
choice_d: A copy of the owner's driver's license alone, with nothing else
explanation: LDWF requires a completed Boat Registration/Boat and Motor Title Application together with original ownership documentation to process a title.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: An incorrect or missing hull identification number (HIN) on a vessel is significant in Louisiana because it:
choice_a: Automatically voids insurance nationwide regardless of state
choice_b: Is only relevant for vessels used exclusively in saltwater
choice_c: Can trigger a titling requirement to establish and correct the vessel's identity in LDWF's records
choice_d: Has no effect on registration or titling in Louisiana
explanation: A vessel with an incorrect or missing HIN falls into one of the categories LDWF requires to be titled, since the HIN is the vessel's unique identifier for registration and law-enforcement purposes.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)

question: Which state agency is responsible for Louisiana's vessel registration and titling program?
choice_a: The Louisiana Department of Motor Vehicles
choice_d: The Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries (LDWF)
explanation: LDWF, not a motor-vehicle agency, administers Louisiana's boat registration and titling program, reflecting the agency's overall role in managing the state's boating safety and waterway programs.
source_note: LDWF, Title or Register Your Boat (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat)
